turn_text: When Senator Tim Caine turned 60, he decided to take on a unique challenge, hike more than 500 miles of the Appalachian Trail in Virginia, bike the Blue Ridge Parkway and the Skyline Drive in the Commonwealth, and paddle the length of the
River. So I feel like I learned a lot about Virginia and I learned a lot about Virginians and I learned a lot about myself.

Cain completed the quest over three years during breaks from his responsibilities in the U.S. Senate, and the result is a new book, Walk, Ride, Paddle, A Life Outside. Recently, I sat down with Cain in Washington, D.C. to talk about his journey and the book it produced, and we started where it started with an idea.

Joe, when I was running for reelection in 2018, I turned 60 and I like to mark milestones, but it wasn't a good year to mark a milestone because I had a campaign to run. But I just decided when the campaigns over, win or lose, I'm going to do something to celebrate turning 60 and 25 years in public life for my first city council race. Campaign finished and maybe Thanksgiving, just a few weeks later. I came up with this idea of create and then complete a Virginia nature triathlon. I was inspired a little bit, as you know, my wife's family's from Roanoke. Anne's older sister, Taylor, has long lived in upstate New York with her husband, who's from the Syracuse area. And New York has this thing called the 46ers, 46 peaks in the Adirondacks higher than 4,000 feet. And families will take this on as a life challenge over the course of their life to hike all of them. Taylor and John had done it with their kids and their dogs and I joined them on a couple. And I just thought, you know what, Virginia needs a quest like this. But what would the Virginia version of it be? And as soon as I ask myself that question, it really just sprung into my head, the Virginia nature triathlon. Hype the whole Virginia portion of the Appalachian Trail from Harper's Ferry to Tennessee. Bicycle the whole Virginia portion of the Blue Ridge Parkway and Skyline Drive from the North Carolina line all the way to Front Royal. And then canoe the whole James River from Iron Gate in Allegheny all the way to the Chesapeake Bay. And so I thought, okay, these are three epic Virginia journeys. I love being in the outdoors. I've done little parts of them over the course of my now 40 years in Virginia. But let me embrace them all as a challenge, see if I can do them, challenge myself, write them up, and then if I could get somebody to publish it, maybe encourage other Virginians to do the same. So it was sort of six years start to finish from having the idea to doing the three trips, to writing the book up, to finding an agent, finding a publisher, and then seeing it in bookstores. It was six years, but it was a love letter to Virginia. I realized that as I was writing the very end of the book. I moved here to get married to this Roenoker in 1984, who is a great outdoors woman, and just as much as I love the outdoors and does too. As you know, in the Senate, we usually are in session about 36 weeks a year, then for 60 weeks, we're in recess. I thought, you know, maybe over this period, and it took about 30 months to do this. I'm going to travel around Virginia, but I'm going to do it where in hiking shorts would know it and showing up in places where people don't expect me.
